_doc: The voice cast sheet (UPDATE 06 B1, T-101). characters.<game>.<code>.actor = the actor id voicing that character (a list for a group, e.g. the Cousins together); "[ACTOR]" / "[COUSIN_1]" are unfilled placeholders (each still gets its own script as slot_<code>). One actor can voice several characters: give them the same id. actors.<id>: name (shown on the script), contact (optional, never shown), notes. Actor ids are lowercase (voice_inbox/<id>/, voice_scripts/<id>/). Read by tools/voice/make_scripts.py and tools/voice/import.py. Edit this file, then run tools/voice.sh scripts. UPDATE 11 (T-193): characters.<game>.<code>.eleven = the ElevenLabs voice: voice_id, voice_name, source (library | design; a clone only with the actor's consent), design_prompt (Voice Design), language (en de ru pl: the language_code sent), stability, similarity_boost (the only eleven_v4 settings), why (the casting reason), none (a reason the character has no voice), consent_actor (whose consent a clone would need); eleven_by_prefix: per line-id prefix overrides (the relief squads). characters.fp = The Fine Print's speakers (same_as = the Gravelight / B&S voice they share). tools/voice.sh elevenlabs voices / assign / design fill it; docs/VOICES.md.

DUT.name: Sgt. Walter "Dutch" Kowalczyk
DUT.who: Sgt. Dutch Kowalczyk, 34, Pittsburgh: low, gravelly baritone, unhurried, complains to keep going
DUT.voice_notes: Low, gravelly baritone. Pittsburgh vowels ("dahntahn," "yinz" exactly once per map, never more). Unhurried, even in a crisis. / His default register is complaint. He complains the way other men pray: steadily, to keep going. He is never actually panicking. When he goes quiet, the squad worries. / His Polish is kitchen Polish learned from an old woman: wrong genders, wrong cases, a grandmother's accent. Read it confidently and wrong. Wren corrects him; he never learns. / Softens noticeably around Wren. Talks to the dead Gängers like disappointed relatives.

eleven.design_prompt: An American man of thirty-four from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in the 1940s: a low, gravelly baritone with a working-class Western Pennsylvania accent, unhurried and dry, a tired army sergeant who grumbles to keep his men going. Close, natural, warm.
eleven.why: Pittsburgh: a Polish-American steelworker's son, 34. Low, gravelly baritone, Western Pennsylvania vowels, unhurried, grumbles to keep the men going; under U11 more tired and frightened, gallows humour thinning.

PEG.name: Lt. Margaret "Peg" Ashworth
PEG.who: Lt. Peg Ashworth, 29, SOE: Received Pronunciation, clipped and precise, never raises her voice
PEG.voice_notes: Received Pronunciation, clipped, precise. Never raises her voice. The worse things get, the more politely she speaks. In a crisis she sounds bored. / Sardonic understatement is her armor: a horde is "a spot of bother." She swears rarely, and when she does it's devastating. / When she's lying, she gets *more* precise, not less. The actor should play the LANTERN hints as tiny, nearly invisible pauses. / Professional fascination with explosives, said with unsettling warmth.

eleven.design_prompt: A British woman of twenty-nine, a 1940s Special Operations officer: crisp upper-class Received Pronunciation, clipped and precise, cool, dry and controlled, never raising her voice.
eleven.why: Posh English: SOE lieutenant, 29, Received Pronunciation, clipped and precise, never raises her voice; the worse things get the more politely she speaks.

DEA.name: Cpl. Elijah "Deacon" Brooks
DEA.who: Cpl. Deacon Brooks, 26, Louisiana: warm tenor, soft-spoken, a preacher's rhythm
DEA.voice_notes: Warm Louisiana tenor, soft-spoken, with a preacher's sense of rhythm he inherited and resists. When he gets going, he can't help preaching a little and then catches himself. / Talks to machines like livestock: "Easy now, girl," "Come on, mule." Never condescending to people. / His blues lines are his own, half-sung, made up on the spot. They should sound like real field blues: AAB form, plain words, bent notes. / Quietly funny. His jokes land half a beat late and he enjoys them more than anyone.

eleven.design_prompt: A young African-American man of twenty-six from rural Louisiana in the 1940s: a warm, soft-spoken tenor with a gentle Southern accent and the measured rhythm of a preacher's son; calm, kind, steady under fear.
eleven.why: Soft Southern: a Louisiana preacher's son, 26, warm soft-spoken tenor with a preacher's rhythm he resists; the quiet theological voice, a line at a time, never a sermon.

WRN.name: Zofia "Wren" Nowak
WRN.who: Wren (Zofia Nowak), 24, Home Army: fluent English learned from British radio, a Polish accent, economical and deadpan
WRN.voice_notes: A Polish speaker with fluent but accented English (learned from British radio and an SOE liaison). Clipped, economical, never wasted words. / Dark humor delivered completely deadpan. She doesn't laugh at her own jokes. / Precise about numbers. She counts out loud under her breath: "sześćdziesiąt dwa... sześćdziesiąt trzy." / Fury runs under everything. It surfaces rarely and frighteningly, mostly about the lab, the tanks, and the forced laborers. / Softens only with Dutch, whom she treats like an embarrassing uncle.

eleven.design_prompt: A young Polish woman of twenty-four, a 1940s resistance fighter, speaking fluent English with a clear Polish accent learned from British radio: low, economical, deadpan, watchful and controlled.
eleven.why: Polish-accented English: Home Army, 24, English learned from British radio, economical and deadpan; she knows the NKVD. Polish words in Polish.

JAK.name: Jakub Ostrowski
JAK.who: Jakub Ostrowski, 44, Silesian salt hewer: English learned late and well enough, an older Polish voice, calm and wry
JAK.voice_notes: Calm, wry, polite. Slow, careful English learned from a German foreman and Polish newspapers; Polish when it matters (shouting, praying, his wife's name), always with the English beside it in the subtitle. / He has seen worse than zombies and isn't impressed by them. Dry humour about himself, never about the dead. / Never raises his voice except at the breakout. Under fire he stays steady.
